speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension; to understand the underlying cause, can you tell me if you have noticed any vomiting, especially if it comes up forcefully or looks like a mixture of food and saliva? Also, has anyone noticed if your belly looks different, like a bulge on one side?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the tenderness and distension are concerning. Has the baby passed any stool recently, and if so, does it contain blood or mucus? Additionally, have you noticed any visible bulges or swelling in the groin or scrotum?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: I'm glad to hear there are no signs of infection. Since the baby is fussy and has abdominal distension without recent stool changes, could you tell me exactly what the stool looks like when he does pass it, and have you noticed any clicking or high-pitched sounds in his belly? Also, does he seem to pass gas easily?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Volvulus (midgut torsion) or high-grade intestinal obstruction.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.
